title: Fast Approximate Bayesian Inference through Bayesian Optimization Sequential Surrogate (BOSS)
text: basic example shows solve simple problem 1-D. Assume true (log) marginal likelihood given following sinusoidal function: can use boss function approximate (log) marginal likelihood function, specifying objective function, dimension problem, bounds BO optimization. alpha parameter controls level essential support, h controls target fill-distance design points.  advanced applications, user can also manually perform step BOSS algorithm, shown :
code: library(BOSS) f1d <- function(x) sin(0.5*pi*x) # A automatic implementation br2 <- boss(f1d, D = 1,              modal_opts = list(lower = 0, upper = 2),             alpha = 0.05, h = 0.1, verbose = 1) #> Stage 1: Bayesian Optimization via Mode-Seeking Surrogate (BOSS) started. #> Stage 1: BOSS finished. #> Total time taken: 1.35 seconds. #> Start updating Hessian at the mode... #> Hessian updated in  0  seconds. #> Stage 2: Fill-in to target spacing h =  0.1  #> fill in: added 21 point(s). #> Final update completed in  0.02  seconds. plot(br2) # A manual implementation br <- BOSS:::BOSS_modal(func = f1d, D = 1,                         lower = 0, upper = 2,                         update_step = 5,                         max_iter = 20,                         verbose = 1) #> Stage 1: Bayesian Optimization via Mode-Seeking Surrogate (BOSS) started. #> Stage 1: BOSS finished. #> Total time taken: 1.12 seconds. br <- update_hessian(br) br <- compute_essential_support(br, alpha=0.05) br <- construct_essential_designs(br) br <- compute_fill_in(br) br <- fill_in(br, h = 0.1, verbose = 1, max_add = 100) #> fill in: added 19 point(s). br_update <- update_boss(br) plot(br_update)

title: Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) Acquisition Function — UCB
text: Numeric vector UCB values (higher better). Internally returns \(-\mu(x) - \sqrt{\beta\,\Sigma(x)}\)   minimizing corresponds maximizing classic UCB acquisition \(\mu + \sqrt{\beta\,\sigma^2}\).

title: Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) Acquisition Function — UCB
text: exploration–exploitation tradeoff parameter \(\beta\) set $$\beta = 2\log\bigl(D^2\pi^2/(6\,d)\bigr).$$ function calls predict_gp obtain posterior mean \(\mu(x)\) variance \(\sigma^2(x)\), computes $$   \mathrm{UCB}(x) \;=\; \mu(x) \;+\;\sqrt{\beta\,\sigma^2(x)}. $$

title: Compute Gaussian Process Log-Likelihood (with Optional Quadratic Mean) — compute_like
code: compute_like(   length_scale,   x,   y,   signal_var,   noise_var,   D,   quad = FALSE,   nu = Inf )

title: Compute Gaussian Process Log-Likelihood (with Optional Quadratic Mean) — compute_like
text: length_scale Positive numeric scalar vector length-scales dimension. x Numeric vector matrix training inputs (rows = observations). y Numeric vector training responses. signal_var Positive numeric scalar specifying GP signal variance (\(\sigma^2\)). noise_var Positive numeric scalar specifying observation noise variance. D Integer. Dimensionality input space (number columns x). quad Logical; FALSE (default), assume zero-mean GP. TRUE, include mean function \(\beta_0 + x^\top \beta_1 + (x \otimes x)^\top \beta_2\). nu Positive numeric specifying smoothness parameter Matérn kernel. Defaults Inf, selecting Squared Exponential kernel.

title: Compute Gaussian Process Log-Likelihood (with Optional Quadratic Mean) — compute_like
text: numeric scalar giving negative log-likelihood (additive constant).   Extremely large values (\(10^{20}\)) returned computation produces NaN, NA,   infinite results.

title: Compute Gaussian Process Log-Likelihood (with Optional Quadratic Mean) — compute_like
text: Zero-mean GP (quad = FALSE): Build covariance \(C = K_{xx} + \sigma_n^2 \) via   cov_generator. Compute Cholesky factor \(L L^\top = C\). Log-determinant: \(\log\det(C) = 2\sum\log(\mathrm{diag}(L))\). Precision \(Q = C^{-1} = \texttt{chol2inv}(L)\). . Negative log-likelihood:   $$\frac{1}{2}\,y^\top Q\,y \;-\; \log\det(Q) \;-\;\sum \log\bigl[\text{LogNormal}(\texttt{length_scale}\mid \texttt{prior_l})\bigr]$$ GP quadratic mean (quad = TRUE): Construct design matrix \(X = [1,\,x,\,\mathrm{unique}(x \otimes x)]\). Build \(C = K_{xx} + \sigma^2_n \) precision \(Q\). Form marginal precision \(S = X^\top Q X\) invert via Cholesky. Compute two quadratic terms:   \(\tfrac12\,y^\top Q\,y\) \(\tfrac12\,y^\top Q X S^{-1} X^\top Q\,y\). Combine log-determinants \(Q\) \(S^{-1}\) log-prior   yield final negative log-likelihood.

what: Estimate Hessian at a point based on sattered data — estimate_hessian
title: Estimate Hessian at a point based on sattered data — estimate_hessian

title: Estimate Hessian at a point based on sattered data — estimate_hessian
text: x numeric vector length D specifying point estimate Hessian. X nXD (\(n \geq {D+2\choose 2}\)) matrix giving locations neighboring points around x (can contain x). y numeric vector length n giving function evaluation X. bw positive real number giving kernel bandwidth locally weighted polynomial regression. Default 1. kernel character string specifying type kernel. one "Epanech" (Default), "RBF", "Tri-cube", "Triangular".

title: Estimate Hessian at a point based on sattered data — estimate_hessian
text: DxD matrix giving estimate Hessian x.

title: Estimate Hessian at a point based on sattered data — estimate_hessian
text: method performs weighted least squares fit local quadratic polynomial centered point \(x\). basis consists monomials total degree 2: $$ \phi(z) = [1, z_1, \dots, z_d, z_1^2, z_1 z_2, \dots, z_d^2]^\top $$ \(z_i = X_i - x_i\) centered design matrix. Kernel weights computed : $$ w_i = K\left(\frac{\|X_i - x\|}{h}\right) $$ \(K(\cdot)\) chosen kernel function. Supported kernels include: - Epanechnikov (default): \(K(r) = \frac{3}{4}(1 - r^2)_+\) - RBF: \(K(r) = \exp\left(-\frac{1}{2} r^2\right)\) - Tri-cube: \(K(r) = (1 - r^3)^3_+\) - Triangular: \(K(r) = (1 - r)_+\) design matrix \(\Phi\) built evaluating degree-0, 1, 2 monomials centered design point. weighted normal equations solved: $$ \hat{\beta} = (\Phi^\top W \Phi)^{-1} \Phi^\top W y $$ estimated Hessian matrix formed applying second-order derivative operators \(D^\alpha\) basis origin: $$ H_{ij} = \sum_{k=1}^N y_k \cdot a_k^{(\alpha)}, \quad \text{} \alpha = e_i + e_j $$ \(^{(\alpha)} = W \Phi (\Phi^\top W \Phi)^{-1} D^\alpha \phi(0)\). function ensures output matrix \(H\) symmetric construction.

what: Fill-in essential support with a Sobol-sequence — fill_in
title: Fill-in essential support with a Sobol-sequence — fill_in
text: Given boss object essential_support essential_design_points$x_original, function approximately fill-Sobol-sequence essential support filter existing design points: Based required fill-distance h, estimate required number quasi-uniform design points   $$     n \;=\; \max\Bigl\{\texttt{n\_sample\_max},\;                      2\,\mathrm{Vol}(\text{Original box})\;\big/\;h^{D}\Bigr\}.   $$ Generate Sobol-sequence within original box. Truncate Sobol-sequence outside ellipsoid. Compute distance existing design points Sobol-sequence remove Sobol-candidates within h existing points. Add maximum max_add number selected fill-Sobol-candidates optimal covering ellipsoid ensured. Recompute new fill-based selected Sobol existing design points.

title: Update Mode Hessian for a boss Object (with PSD check) — update_hessian
text: function numerically computes hessian mode obtained boss Object using three different strategies: 1. Default: Locally weighted polynomial regression (local.poly): given specified accuracy level local.poly.args$eps, function first draws circle radius local.poly.args$eps/2 around mode boss object check many boss design points within circle. number \(n = (D+2)(D+1)\), additional uniformly distributed design points added within circle reach \(n\) evaluate additional points boss_result$objective_function. Combining design points circle, estimate Hessian boss mode locally weighted polynomial regression using estimate_hessian(). default kernel bw argument estimate_hessian() set local.poly.args$eps / 2*D^0.4. local.poly.args$eps = NULL, obtained $$\epsilon = \frac{1}{4\sqrt{\text{Tr}(-H_{GP})}},$$ \(H_{GP}\) hessian boss mode computed numDeriv::hessian() GP surrogate boss_result$surrogate. 2. Brute-force numerical hessian (num.obj): directly estimate hessian boss mode via numDeriv::hessian() using boss_result$objective_function. 3. Numerical hessian based GP surrogate (num.GP): estimate hessian boss mode via numDeriv::hessian() using boss_result$surrogate. Note local.poly balances theoretical accuracy computational budget. num.obj computationally intense num.GP cheapest, theoretical guarantee. addition, noise evaluation boss_result$objective_function, recommend users use local.poly num.GP. Otherwise, numDeriv::hessian() based boss_result$objective_function highly unstable.
